_why: ADR 0071's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The table in that ADR was produced by a hand-run loop before the
harness existed. Two of its rows are the ones worth being able to
re-run rather than trust: the citation exemption that would have let
the real fabricated testimonials through, and the record-match that
was satisfied by the table of REMOVED fabrications.
One row of the original table was a no-op that reported a false 'not
caught' -- moving the block delimiters in a direction that changed
nothing, because the block sits above the removal table. The harness
reports INDETERMINATE for a patch that does not change the bytes,
which is the whole reason it exists. That row is deliberately not
reproduced here; F5 below is the corrected version.

mutations.description: the citation exemption reverts to a case-insensitive substring
mutations._note: The near-miss. `Source: Hoare & Pal (1971)` is a citation; `source: "Stanford University"` is a testimonial field. Matched case-insensitively, one rule exempts both -- so the guard would have passed the exact carousel it was written to catch. An exemption added to stop crying wolf had switched off the alarm.
A checklist with nothing on it passes everything. The floor exists so that deleting the list is not a way to pass.

mutations.description: a claim is found but never reported
mutations._note: The silent-detector shape: everything is examined, nothing is said, the run is green.

mutations.description: the whole ENDORSEMENTS.md counts as the allowlist again
mutations._note: The live hole, not a hypothetical: the file's table of REMOVED fabrications contains rows like `| Stanford University |`, so `"| Stanford" in recorded` matched it. Four of the five institutions were already exempt on every public page -- the document written to condemn them was excusing them.
mutations.find:
if _BLOCK_START not in text or _BLOCK_END not in text:
        return None
    start = text.index(_BLOCK_START) + len(_BLOCK_START)
    return text[start : text.index(_BLOCK_END, start)]

mutations.description: a missing allowlist block reads as an empty, permissive one
mutations._note: The corrected form of the original table's no-op row. 'No block' must not mean 'no rules' -- deleting the checklist is the easiest way to pass a checklist.
mutations.find:
if _BLOCK_START not in text or _BLOCK_END not in text:
        return None
mutations.replace:
if _BLOCK_START not in text or _BLOCK_END not in text:
        return ""
